sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg & Roger Blench. 2026. The peopling of the Muri Mountains, Northern Nigeria: evidence from linguistics and ethnography. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online (AAeO) 2026, 47 pp. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2026_12031 (published 2026-02-03).
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnohistorical synthesis of the Muri Mountains area (Karim Lamido / Lau LGAs); sec. 3.3.2.2 'Bandawa' (p. 22): 'The Bandawa (who call themselves Yishu; Meek NAK SNP 17 - 21577:30), are linguistically a part of the Shoo-Minda-Nye sub-group [bcv] of the Wurbo cluster', followed by migration traditions (source: typescript 'History of Bandawa People in Karim Lamido L.G.A.', n.d.); Kunini appears only in jihad history, Lau under 3.5 Central Sudanic (Kaba Laka). No linguistic data, no phonology; 'tone'/'phonology' in the text concern Dadiya, Kyak, Yebu, Jen, Waja (reference titles) and Ja…

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry & Mark L. O. Van de Velde. 2020. Nigeria as a linguistic terra incognita: The two languages of Lau. In A. A. Kibrik et al. (eds.), VAProsy jazykoznanija: A megacollection of nanopapers, 322-328. Moscow: Buki Vedi.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4 (p. 327) identifies Lau [law] as a variety of Shoo-Minda-Nye and states that Shimizu (1980a) 'does not provide any linguistic data for the lects spoken in these settlements and only refers to three unpublished wordlists of 42 (Lau), 112 (Bandawa) and 102 (Minda) items collected around 1930 by Charles K. Meek'; gives five tone-marked Lau words (Table 1); no prosody.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 421 'Shoo-Minda-Nye cluster'. (text already held by the project)
sources.note: Nothing; entry gives location (Taraba, Karim Lamido LGA), 10,000 (SIL), classification (Wurbo cluster), members Shoo (Banda/Bandawa), Minda (Jinleri), Nye (Kunini), 'Source(s) Leger (1990); Kleinewillinghoefer (1992); Refs. Shimizu (1980)'; no grammar/phonology refs listed.

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry, Mark Van de Velde, Tope Olagunju & Bitrus Andrew. 2017. Results of the first AdaGram survey in Adamawa and Taraba States, Nigeria. Paper (slides) presented at CALL 47, Leiden, 28 August 2017. 33 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Slides 'LAU: LAU': Shimizu (1980:42) classifies Lau with Bandawa and Minda 'but provides no data'; 'Lau is probably Jukunoid, indeed'; 'We later collected additional data with a speaker of Lau in Ilorin.. that we still need to process.'
sources.venue: Paper (slides) presented at CALL 47, Leiden, 28 August

sources.citation: Ethnologue, 14th ed. (Grimes ed. 2000), web entry BCV Shoo-Minda-Nye (Internet Archive copy 2001-11-09).
sources.note: Nothing; dialects SHOO (BANDA, BANDAWA), MINDA (JINLERI), NYE (KUNINI); 'Called Bakula together with Como Karim, Munga, Jiru, and Jessi'.

sources.citation: Meek, C. K. 1931. A Sudanese Kingdom: An ethnographical study of the Jukun-speaking peoples of Nigeria. London: Kegan Paul. (archive.org scanned, already held by the project)
sources.note: p. 35: the people of Lau, Bandawa, Kwinini (Kunini), Minda 'do not speak Jukun as their mother tongue. Their language is of a primitive monosyllabic type, but the vocabulary shows a number of resemblances to Jukun'. Minda otherwise only in a comparative word table. Nothing on stress or tone for this language.

sources.citation: The Word for the World International & The Word for the World Nigeria. n.d. [c. 2020s]. Bandawa Language Project (BLP): Scripture portions in Shoo (Bandawa) / Shoo-Minda-Nye [bcv], e.g. Matiyu (Matthew). YouVersion Bible id 4448; listed on find.bible as BCVWFW.
sources.note: No phonology content: running scripture text only (Matthew 2:1-5 read). Practical orthography uses ɓ, ə, ɔ and nasal tildes (byə̃ng, nangzhĩ); no systematic tone diacritics and no orthography statement or reading guide is published with it. A TWFTW translator-training phonology write-up may exist but is not online.

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry & Mark Van de Velde (LLACAN, AdaGram project). Unpublished field data on Lau (Shoo-Minda-Nye), collected 2016-2017 (survey in Lau town and follow-up with a speaker in Ilorin), 'still to be processed' per the 2017 slides.

sources.note: The only modern first-hand linguistic data on any Shoo-Minda-Nye lect; any future phonological sketch (tone, and whether there is word stress) would come from here. Worth asking the authors directly whether a sketch or tone/stress notes exist.

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. c. 1921-1931. Unpublished vocabularies of Bandawa (112 items), Minda (102 items) and Lau (42 items); 'Wurbo, 14 items, 1921, Linguistic Notes II.2' (cited by Shimizu 1980b: xiv). Manuscripts, presumably among the Meek papers (Bodleian Library, Oxford / Nigerian National Archives).

sources.note: The only other primary lexical record of the language; wordlists of that era occasionally carry accent marks or a note on stress, though a prosodic statement is unlikely.
